cards.explanation: The answer is an upright heart. Elihu, the young man now speaking to Job, says it plainly: “My words are from an upright heart, and my lips speak sincerely what I know.” He puts that on the table before he gets into his speech. It's his own claim about himself, so keep listening to see what he does with it.

The answer is that Elihu invites Job to refute him if he can. He says, “Refute me if you can; prepare your case and confront me.” He's inviting Job to push back, not just nod along. That's a man who's ready for a real conversation. Honestly, I've never invited anybody to argue with my cookie recipes, so I'm a little impressed.

The answer is True. Elihu tells Job, “Surely no fear of me should terrify you; nor will my hand be heavy upon you.” He's telling Job there's no need to be afraid of him. He's saying he won't come down hard on him.

The answer is enemy. Elihu quotes Job saying, “Yet God finds occasions against me; He counts me as His enemy.” Those are heavy words, friends, and Elihu repeats them right back to him. Elihu is about to answer them.
The answer is False. Elihu says, “Behold, you are not right in this matter.” He doesn't agree with what he just quoted from Job. He says he's going to answer him.

The answer is that God is greater than man. Elihu says, “I will answer you, for God is greater than man.” That's the reason he gives for answering Job. It's a short sentence, but it carries the weight for everything else Elihu says here. I think of it as the top of the whole speech.

The answer is nothing. Elihu asks, “Why do you complain to Him that He answers nothing a man asks?” He's questioning the complaint itself. He's about to say God does speak, in one way and another (Job 33:14).

The answer is through a dream or a vision. Elihu says God speaks “In a dream, in a vision in the night, when deep sleep falls upon men as they slumber on their beds…” So here the night is when God speaks. People are asleep, and that's when He opens their ears (Job 33:16).

The answer is pride. Elihu says God sends these warnings “…to turn a man from wrongdoing and keep him from pride…” So the warnings aren't random. Elihu ties them to turning a man around, and pride is the thing he names.

The answer is False. Elihu says the warnings are “…to preserve his soul from the Pit and his life from perishing by the sword.” Preserving is the goal, friends. The warnings are about keeping him from the Pit.

The answer is True. Elihu says the man's pain is so bad “…that he detests his bread, and his soul loathes his favorite food.” Even the best thing on the table doesn't appeal to him. That's a rough picture of someone hurting.

The answer is his ransom. The messenger says, “Spare him from going down to the Pit; I have found his ransom…” A ransom is the price that sets someone free. The man isn't spared because he talked his way out. Someone found the ransom for him.

The answer is child. Elihu says, “…then his flesh is refreshed like a child’s; he returns to the days of his youth.” After the wasting away, his flesh is refreshed. It's a big turnaround from the Pit.

The answer is that he had truly done wrong. His song says, “I have sinned and perverted what was right; yet I did not get what I deserved.” He sings it in front of people, and that takes some nerve. He doesn't hide that he sinned. He also says he didn't get what he deserved.

The answer is False. The man sings, “He redeemed my soul from going down to the Pit, and I will live to see the light.” The song hands the redeeming to Someone else. He also looks ahead to living to see the light.

The answer is False. Elihu says God does these things “…to bring back his soul from the Pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of life.” Bringing the man back is the reason in the text. Nothing in the verse is about testing how much he can take.

The answer is to clear his name. Elihu says, “But if you have something to say, answer me; speak up, for I would like to vindicate you.” To vindicate is to clear someone's name. He says he'd like to do that for Job, friends. So he leaves the door open.
